findings.title: Receipt polling accepts a receipt without binding it to the requested transaction
findings.status: Affects main and release; corrected in integration; PR298 fixes hash binding only, retaining permissive status handling
findings.condition: The selected RPC returns an inconsistent receipt: the transactionHash is missing or differs from the requested hash, or status is an integer outside the two defined outcomes.
findings.evidence: The older pollReceipt reads destination, status and blockNumber without validating transactionHash, and maps every status except 1 to reverted. The latest integration requires a valid matching transactionHash and status exactly 0 or 1.
findings.impact: Payment confirmation or revert presentation can be attributed to a receipt that does not identify the requested transaction. This is a boundary-validation defect under inconsistent RPC data, not proof of chain-state forgery or theft.
findings.fix: Retain the strict hash and status validation from the integration version across all shipped branches; retain the original known transaction hash and an unresolved outcome when validation fails.
findings.acceptance: Read-only/unit validation should establish that missing or mismatched receipt identity and out-of-domain status cannot produce success/reverted, while the original transaction remains trackable. No live endpoint or transaction is required.

findings.title: Malformed ERC20 simulation output is classified as a successful dry run
findings.status: Affects main, release and integration; corrected only in inspected PR305 head
findings.condition: An ERC20-style call is simulated with expectBool=true and the RPC returns nonempty even-length hex that is not a canonical ABI boolean.
findings.evidence: The older helper rejects only a 32-byte zero result. Every other syntactically hex result returns ok. PR305 classifies nonempty output with the wrong width or value as unavailable.
findings.impact: The interface can omit the unavailable-simulation warning despite lacking a meaningful affirmative simulation result. A dry run is not a guarantee of execution, and the product deliberately allows unavailable simulation with a warning; this finding does not demonstrate a bypass that directly moves funds to an unintended recipient.
findings.fix: Integrate the PR305 canonical boolean check without losing legacy empty-return compatibility or the explicit false-return refusal.
findings.acceptance: Validate that canonical true is ok, canonical false refuses, empty legacy output follows its documented policy, and all other nonempty boolean-domain output is unavailable. Verify caller warning propagation for both submitted and unknown-after-handoff outcomes.

findings.title: Main sweep operations do not revoke an in-flight signing review when visible inputs change
findings.status: Affects main-derived sweep implementation; corrected in release/integration
findings.condition: A sweep action has begun with a valid session, then its destination, mode or displayed review context is changed while preflight/signing is awaiting completion.
findings.evidence: Main guard captures session/authEpoch only. The main direct/relayed helpers are called without a UI assertReviewCurrent capability; directSweep checks the seller session but not the current UI review before signing and handoff. The editable destination remains available while busy. Latest view binds balance and quote scopes, aborts on context changes and passes assertReviewCurrent through the helper to handoff.
findings.impact: A transaction can continue using the earlier captured destination/context after the interface presents changed input. This is stale consent, not arbitrary recipient injection. No fund-loss magnitude is asserted.
findings.fix: Preserve scope-bound cancellation and review guards from release/integration, checking before and after asynchronous preparation, immediately before signing, and before handoff. Preserve truthful tracking once a handoff has already occurred.
findings.acceptance: With local stubbed dependencies, changing a review field or leaving the view before handoff must prevent later signing/handoff; a response after an actual handoff must keep the original transaction/order tracked. Native confirmation must remain single-use, scoped and time-bounded.

findings.title: Page hiding does not revoke pending local imports in the main camera/import component
findings.condition: A paste or image import remains pending when the document becomes hidden, with no active camera.
findings.evidence: Main visibilityChanged invokes stop only for a camera; visible does not check document visibility; deliver invokes the consumer callback before its first cancellation/visibility check. Latest also stops localImport work, includes document visibility in visible(), and checks before the callback.
findings.impact: An import consumer can receive content after the page has hidden and the intended local action lifetime should have ended. Consumer-specific checks may limit downstream effects; no secret exfiltration or unauthorized signing was established here.
findings.fix: Retain the latest cancellation and pre-delivery checks; consumers must also recheck their supplied signal before committing any asynchronous state.
findings.acceptance: Pending paste and image operations must be cancelled when hidden; becoming visible must require a fresh user action. Hidden/aborted callbacks must not commit imported state.

findings.title: parseUnits runtime arguments are not validated in main/integration
findings.classification: Robustness; no demonstrated external security reachability
findings.status: Affects main, release and integration; corrected in inspected PR301/303 heads
findings.condition: A caller violates the TypeScript boundary with a non-string amount or non-integer/out-of-range decimal precision. Production callers reviewed generally supply strings and configured decimal precision.
findings.evidence: The old function calls text.trim(), BigInt(decimals), exponentiation and padEnd without runtime argument checks, despite documenting undefined for unexpected input. The standalone correction bounds decimal precision to 0..36 and validates type before arithmetic.
findings.impact: Unexpected exceptions or excessive work are possible at the utility boundary. No network-controlled production input path to unbounded decimal precision was established; do not present this as a remotely exploitable denial of service.
findings.fix: Retain the narrow type/range guard in PR301/303.
findings.acceptance: Unexpected runtime type or precision is rejected predictably without coercion, rounding, excessive allocation or arithmetic exceptions. Valid configured amounts preserve exact bigint behavior.

findings.title: QR classification helpers rely on compile-time union types in older versions
findings.classification: Defensive runtime hardening; no demonstrated external exposure
findings.status: Main lacks unknown-key guards; release adds own-key checks; integration/PR290 also validates string type
findings.condition: A runtime caller supplies a value outside QrKind/QrPayloadType, including inherited object keys or non-string property keys. Reviewed normal callers use typed constants.
findings.evidence: Main reads PAYLOAD_KIND[type] directly and constructs class names without validation. Intermediate own-property validation still permits property-key coercion. Latest checks string type and an own key before classification.
findings.impact: Unexpected classification, missing handling rules or rendering failures are possible for invalid internal input. No demonstrated route lets imported QR data select a privileged secret-handling kind; do not claim key disclosure.
findings.fix: Preserve latest runtime string and own-key checks and keep secret/bearer handling stronger than generic caution flags.
findings.acceptance: Out-of-domain and non-string kind/payload arguments fail before coercion or property access. Legitimate secret/bearer payloads retain their handling regardless of caution flags.

findings.title: Older multipart QR encoding silently normalizes ill-formed Unicode input
findings.classification: Encoding integrity; production reachability not established
findings.condition: toMultipart receives a string containing an unpaired UTF16 surrogate. Normal invoice/key payload producers reviewed produce structured encoded text.
findings.evidence: Main delegates straight to TextEncoder, which replaces such code units. Latest rejects them before encoding.
findings.impact: The multipart payload can differ from the caller-provided text; no valid signed invoice/key corruption flow was established. This is a library integrity edge case rather than a demonstrated remote vulnerability.
findings.fix: Retain the latest pre-encoding rejection and consistent byte-preservation behavior across single and multipart QR paths.
findings.acceptance: Ill-formed Unicode is rejected before generating parts, while valid Unicode round-trips byte-for-byte.

retired_or_transferred.topic: Privacy defaults in CreateInvoice and ReceiptPanel
retired_or_transferred.status: Observed correction, not independently claimed as a new vulnerability
